title: gitiup run manifest (v1)
description:
The signed payload of a gitiup attestation: what ran, on what change, in what environment, with what outcome. Normative alongside ADR-0001 (docs/adr/0001-attestation-encoding-hash-and-signature.md); the ADR decides the encoding of these bytes (canonical JSON, ADR-0001 D1) and what each field means, this schema says which fields exist.

A few rules are enforced by the Rust reader rather than by JSON Schema and are noted with x-gitiup-note: no nulls anywhere (an absent field is an omitted key), integers only (i64, no floats), object keys in ascending order and duplicate-free, lists marked x-gitiup-sorted required sorted and unique, and every string free of control characters and at most 16384 bytes.

schema_version.description: Manifest format version. Inside the signed payload so a v2 document cannot be checked with v1 rules.

result.description: Everything a faithful re-run reproduces. Its digest is what independent verifiers compare.

claims.description: Who claimed it and when. Signed and policy-checked, never compared for equality between runs.

gitOid.description: A git object name. The algorithm is part of the string so a sha256-object-format repository can be bound without a format change.

microseconds.description: Microseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC. An integer, not an RFC 3339 string, so there is exactly one encoding (ADR-0001 D6).

text.description: A short human-readable string. Never raw control characters; never binary (binary content is referred to by digest).

runId.description: Per-run identifier: 8-32 random bytes as hex.

sorted.x-gitiup-note: Lists carrying x-gitiup-sorted must be sorted ascending and duplicate-free, so two honest producers hash the same bytes. JSON Schema cannot express this; RunResult::normalize() and RunManifest::validate() do.

RunManifest.$comment: Alias of the root document, listed so tooling can address it by name.

inputs.x-gitiup-note: Absent when empty: an empty map is omitted, never null.

secret_names.description: Names of secrets made available. Never their values.

pins.description: Resolved pin for every uses: in the run.

steps.description: Steps in execution order. This is the one order that is meaningful, so it is not sorted.

repo.description: Human-facing repository identity. Not trusted for anything.

commit.description: The commit this run is bound to. An attestation offered against a different commit is refused.

job.description: Job id, when the workflow has more than one.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the workflow file.

oid.description: The source that was executed: a git blob id, or sha256:<hex> of the file bytes when the file is not committed.

payload.description: Digest of the event payload as received. The payload itself stays out of the manifest.

repo.description: owner/name or full URL of the action repository.

commit.description: The immutable commit checked out. A floating ref is not a pin.

ref.description: The ref the user wrote (v4, main). Evidence of what the pin resolved from; never trusted.

provider.description: Backend that ran the job: docker, podman, containerd, shell, simulated.

os_version.description: OS version as the OS reports it (24.04). Kept apart from os because a policy rounds the version and never the id: require-env-match = major rounds this field only (giti-1rs.4).

arch.description: CPU architecture (x86_64, aarch64). Stored in the spelling std::env::consts::ARCH produces; a policy may name it in any spelling because Arch::new canonicalises amd64/arm64 onto it.

fingerprint.description: Derived, not asserted: sha256 of the canonical encoding of this object with fingerprint set to sha256 of the empty string. A fingerprint that does not match the environment described is a validation error.
fingerprint.x-gitiup-note: Must not carry per-machine identity (hostname, uid, build paths): the fingerprint identifies a machine class, and per-machine values would make independent runs incomparable.

reference.description: What was asked for (ubuntu:24.04). Evidence only.

digest.description: What was actually pulled, pinned by digest.

version.description: Version as the tool reports it.

id.description: Step id as written in the workflow, if it had one. Unique when present.

name.description: Step name, or the uses: string.

stdout.description: Digest of the NORMALISED stdout. Raw logs are not part of an attestation (giti-1rs.3).

stepOutcome.description: How the runner classified the step.

digest.description: Digest of the artifact content, or of the manifest for a directory.

runner.description: Runner implementation and version, e.g. gitiup 0.1.0.

normalisation_version.description: Which normalisation rules produced the digests. Results from different versions are not comparable.

sandbox.description: Confinement backend, if any (docker, landlock, none).

tier.description: Provenance tier. In a run manifest the value is simulated or local: quorum is a verdict over several attestations, recorded separately and never self-asserted by one run.

InputValue.description: A scalar input value. Scalars only: a composite value would mean two ways to encode one input.

not_before_us.description: Optional validity lower bound; must not be after claimed_at_us.

not_after_us.description: Optional validity upper bound; must be after claimed_at_us.

verifier_challenge.description: Commit-reveal challenge this submission is bound to (giti-msi.6).

timing.description: Per-step wall-clock evidence, keyed by step id. Outside result on purpose: durations never agree between machines.
timing.x-gitiup-note: Keys should match a steps[].id; they are not constrained to, because a step may be unnamed.

normalisation_diffs.description: What normalisation had to rewrite. Evidence for a dispute; the before side is machine-specific by definition, so it must stay out of result.

annotations.description: Extension point for third-party fields, by convention named x_<producer>_<name>. Strings only, so an extension can never be richer than a typed field.

kind.description: timestamp, path, hostname, locale, ansi, line-ending, ...

after.description: Text after rewriting (may be a placeholder).
